claims.text: In February 2025, a demo of JupyterLab 4.4 was presented by Mike Krassowski during the Jupyter Community Call.

citations.quote:
* **Mike Krassowski** JupyterLab 4.4 demo


## Other Links Shared

Fragment Identification Syntax for Jupyter: https://github.com/jupyter/nbformat/issues/317

claims.rationale: Correct February demo passage and Mike attribution. Source is an agenda item, so it directly establishes a listed demo; presented during the call is a conventional but stronger summary than an independently confirmed completed presentation. This caveat is not the sole blocking issue.

claims.text: In February 2025, it was reported that the JupyterLab 4.4 beta would be released on that day during the Jupyter Community Call.

citations.quote: * **Mike Krassowski** JupyterLab 4.4 beta will be released today :crossed_fingers:

claims.rationale: Correct beta announcement quote says will be released today. The text preserves would be released on that day. Trailing during the Community Call can be read as the report time or added release-time constraint; only the report time is supported.

claims.text: In June 2025, it was reported that JupyterLab 4.4 and Notebook 7.4 were released during the Jupyter Community Call.
claims.rationale: The source says JupyterLab 4.4 and Notebook 7.4 are out: availability reported at the June meeting. The answer says were released during the Jupyter Community Call, which naturally adds release-event timing not in the source. A charitable reading attaches during to reported, but the statement does not reliably preserve the preregistered distinction between meeting date and release date. Mark as ambiguous temporal overclaim, not independently proved false release history.

case_reviews.completeness: February beta plan and June availability are both addressed using the correct source passages. Nevertheless, the June formulation does not cleanly pass the explicit event-time fidelity gate. No longer repeats v1 claim that both months saw a completed release.
